question: How is primary infertility defined in the clinic?

options.A: Never achieving a pregnancy after twelve months of regular unprotected sex
options.B: Failing to carry a pregnancy past the first trimester
options.C: Failing to conceive within six months of trying
options.D: Having only one child and wanting no more

explanation: Primary infertility means a person or couple has never achieved a pregnancy despite trying with regular unprotected sex for a full year. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T6#BMP224_U4_T6_h1)

question: Which of these describes secondary infertility?

options.A: A newly married couple trying to conceive for six months
options.B: An older woman trying to have her very first baby
options.C: A couple with two children who experienced a sudden miscarriage
options.D: A woman who gave birth before and is now unable to conceive after twelve months of trying

explanation: Secondary infertility applies when a woman has been pregnant successfully in the past, but is currently unable to achieve a new pregnancy after a year of trying. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T6#BMP224_U4_T6_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT part of a basic male fertility check?
explanation: An endometrial biopsy checks the lining of the uterus in the female partner, so it is not used in the initial check of the male partner. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T6#BMP224_U4_T6_h2)

question: A couple comes to the clinic struggling to conceive after fourteen months. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Tell the woman to stop working outside the home
options.B: Refer them immediately for expensive IVF
options.C: Prescribe strong hormone pills to the woman
options.D: Take a detailed medical and reproductive history from both partners

explanation: Care always starts with a thorough history from both partners to help guide the next steps and tests. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T6#BMP224_U4_T6_h2)

question: Why is having a clear referral pathway important for managing infertility?

options.A: It guarantees that every couple will get pregnant naturally
options.B: It permanently removes the midwife from patient care
options.C: It ensures couples see specialists before wasting money on unproven treatments
options.D: It removes the need for any basic clinic tests

explanation: Clear referral pathways guide patients to advanced care smoothly, protecting them from delays and financial exploitation. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T6#BMP224_U4_T6_h3)

question: Which finding during a basic fertility check strongly points to the need for a specialist referral?

options.A: A menstrual cycle lasting twenty-eight days
options.B: Complete blockage in both fallopian tubes
options.D: Feeling a bit tired after a long workday

explanation: Blocked tubes prevent natural fertilization and require advanced surgical help or assisted reproduction available at specialist centers. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T6#BMP224_U4_T6_h3)

question: How do cultural pressures in many communities typically affect couples dealing with infertility?

options.A: They place intense emotional and social pressure, especially on women
options.B: They automatically provide financial support from family
options.C: They encourage couples to seek early professional counselling
options.D: They reduce stress by encouraging adoption

explanation: Societal expectations often link womanhood closely to childbearing, making infertility a source of deep emotional pain and social stigma. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T6#BMP224_U4_T6_h4)

question: A patient cries during a fertility visit, feeling worthless because she has no child. How should the midwife respond?

options.A: Tell her to ignore her family and focus on her career
options.B: Change the subject to check her husband's lab results
options.C: Acknowledge her pain gently and listen to her in a safe space
options.D: Tell her to stop crying because stress ruins ovulation

explanation: Active listening and emotional support are key midwifery skills for helping patients deal with the grief of infertility. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T6#BMP224_U4_T6_h4)

question: What is a major goal of community education regarding infertility?

options.A: Correcting myths and showing that fertility involves both partners
options.B: Convincing people that treatment is always too expensive
options.C: Encouraging couples to avoid modern hospitals
options.D: Promoting the idea that infertility only affects women

explanation: Community education aims to clear up false beliefs by teaching that both men and women contribute equally to reproductive health. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T6#BMP224_U4_T6_h5)

question: Why is reducing community stigma around infertility so important for public health?

options.A: It ensures traditional healers handle all treatments
options.B: It removes the need for any laboratory tests
options.C: It encourages couples to seek medical help much earlier
options.D: It stops the natural aging of the reproductive organs

explanation: When stigma goes down, fear drops, which helps couples seek professional medical care without hiding their struggles. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T6#BMP224_U4_T6_h5)
